intro.title: Web Applications That Work as Hard as You Do
paragraphs: A web application is software that runs in the browser: a customer portal, a booking system, an admin dashboard, an online marketplace or a full SaaS product. Unlike a simple <wd>business website</wd> that mostly shows information, a web app lets people log in, enter data, make transactions and get work done, on any device, with nothing to install.

Every web app has two halves. The frontend is everything users see and click, and it needs to be fast, clear and accessible. The backend is the engine behind it: business logic, databases, security, integrations and APIs. We handle both, plus UI/UX design, testing, deployment and maintenance, so you have one accountable team from first sketch to live product.

We build with proven technology such as React, Angular and Next.js on the front end, and Python (Django, Flask), Java, .NET and PHP (Laravel) on the back end, choosing what suits your project rather than what is fashionable. See <work>web apps we have built</work>, explore our <csd>custom software development</csd> or <contact>tell us about your idea</contact>.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.subtitle: Quick answers about web application development.

items.a: Web application development is the process of designing, building, testing and deploying software that runs in a web browser. It includes the frontend users interact with, the backend that handles data and logic, and the hosting that keeps it online.

items.q: What is the difference between a website and a web application?
items.a: A website mainly presents information, such as company pages or a blog. A web application lets users log in, enter data and complete tasks, such as booking, ordering, managing records or using a SaaS product.

items.q: What is frontend and backend development?
items.a: Frontend development builds the part users see and interact with, using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and frameworks like React or Angular. Backend development builds the server, database and business logic behind it, using languages like Python, Java, .NET or PHP.

items.q: Which technology is best for web application development?
items.a: It depends on your project. React or Angular are strong frontend choices; Python with Django suits data-heavy apps and fast MVPs, Java and .NET suit large enterprise systems, and PHP with Laravel is cost-effective for many business apps. We recommend the stack after understanding your needs.

items.q: How much does web app development cost and how long does it take?
items.a: A simple web app or MVP typically costs $5,000 to $15,000 and takes 4 to 8 weeks. Business web apps cost $15,000 to $50,000 over 2 to 4 months, and enterprise or SaaS platforms start around $50,000.

items.q: Can you build a web app and a mobile app together?
items.a: Yes. We can build a progressive web app that works like a mobile app, or native and hybrid iOS and Android apps that share the same backend as your web app, saving time and cost.
